skill.name: async-python-patterns
skill.description: Guides Python developers through asyncio, async and await, concurrent I/O, task orchestration, rate limiting, and testing patterns.
skill.summary: Build reliable async Python services with practical asyncio patterns.
skill.author: ActiveInferenceInstitute

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and normal asyncio tutorial examples. No prompt injection or executable malware behavior was found, but one semantic issue remains: the async database example teaches interpolated SQL that should be parameterized.

remediation.issue: Unsafe SQL query construction in the async database example
remediation.suggestion: Replace f-string SQL with parameterized queries or placeholders, and explain that untrusted values must never be interpolated into SQL.

remediation.issue: Sample URLs may be copied into runnable code
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholder and httpbin URLs as examples, and advise users to use trusted endpoints, timeouts, and rate limits.
No security fix is required for the Markdown backticks, but keep the skill free of install hooks or executable scripts.

Resources that support `async with` for proper cleanup.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe SQL Query Construction in Example
semantic_findings.description: The async database example builds SQL statements with f-strings that include user_id. If copied into real code with untrusted values, this can teach SQL injection-prone query construction.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly interpolate a variable into SELECT statements. The database client is simulated and the example passes an integer literal, so the risk is insecure guidance rather than active exploit code.

content.value_statement: Async Python code can fail when tasks, timeouts, and blocking calls are handled incorrectly. This skill provides practical asyncio patterns for reliable concurrent applications.
actual_capabilities: Explains core asyncio concepts such as event loops, coroutines, tasks, futures, and async context managers.
Shows patterns for gather, create_task, timeouts, cancellation handling, and async iterators.
Provides examples for aiohttp requests, connection pools, WebSocket-style message handling, and async database access.
Covers performance controls such as semaphores, batching, connection pooling, and executor use for blocking work.
Includes common async pitfalls and pytest-asyncio testing examples.
limitations: Does not provide runnable package code, tests, or helper scripts beyond documentation examples.
Uses simulated services and placeholder URLs that must be adapted before production use.
Does not cover every async framework or advanced event loop implementation.
Some database examples need parameterized queries before use with untrusted input.

use_cases.title: Design Async API Handlers
use_cases.description: Plan non-blocking request handlers that coordinate database calls, network calls, and background tasks.

use_cases.title: Improve I/O Workloads
use_cases.description: Refactor serial network or database operations into bounded concurrent workflows with timeouts and error handling.

use_cases.title: Teach Async Foundations
use_cases.description: Use concise examples to explain coroutines, tasks, queues, locks, cancellation, and async testing.

prompt_templates.title: Explain My Coroutine Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of async and await behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the async-python-patterns skill to explain how my coroutine flow works. Identify where tasks are created, awaited, and cleaned up.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor I/O Calls
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert serial I/O into bounded concurrency.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the async-python-patterns skill to refactor this serial I/O workflow into asyncio. Include timeouts, gather usage, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Async Production Risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Check an async service for reliability issues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the async-python-patterns skill to review this async service. Look for blocking calls, missing cancellation handling, unbounded tasks, and weak cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Concurrent Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture for high-throughput async processing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the async-python-patterns skill to design a producer-consumer pipeline with backpressure, rate limits, retries, cancellation, and async tests.

output_examples.input: A developer asks why their async API is slow despite using async functions.
output_examples.output: The skill would point out blocking calls, missing concurrent task scheduling, and lack of timeouts. It would suggest gather, semaphores, and executor use where appropriate.

output_examples.input: A team wants to process many API URLs without overwhelming a service.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend bounded concurrency, connection pooling, response timeouts, and clear failure handling for partial results.

output_examples.input: An educator needs a lesson plan for asyncio basics.
output_examples.output: The skill would organize concepts from coroutines and tasks through queues, locks, cancellation, and testing.

best_practices: Use bounded concurrency with semaphores, queues, or connection pool limits for external services.
Add explicit timeouts, cancellation handling, and cleanup for long-running tasks.
Keep blocking CPU or synchronous I/O work outside the event loop.
anti_patterns: Calling synchronous sleep or blocking libraries inside async functions.
Creating many tasks without limits, cancellation plans, or backpressure.
Building SQL or network requests from untrusted values without validation or parameterization.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design and review async Python applications that use asyncio and concurrent I/O.

faq.question: Does it execute code or install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation with examples and guidance.

faq.question: Which Python features does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers async functions, await, tasks, gather, queues, locks, async iterators, timeouts, and cancellation.

faq.question: Can it help with aiohttp or FastAPI?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns relevant to async HTTP clients, web APIs, and service workloads.

faq.question: Is the sample code production ready?
faq.answer: No. The examples are teaching material and need validation, security hardening, and project-specific integration.

faq.question: Can it help test async code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for pytest-asyncio and timeout-based async tests.
